findings.evidence: p31: "Ch. 2 §2.1.1 (latent video) and Ch. 3 §3.1.1"; p34: "Ch. 4 §4.8 and Ch. 7 §7.8"; p36: "Ch 4 §4.3 quotes this formula verbatim"; p46: "defined in full at Ch 8 §8.3.3"; p146: "developed in Ch 8 §8.7"
findings.issue: Recurring malformed cross-references: the chapter number is repeated after "Ch N". The Preface's own convention says: "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." These pointers violate that rule and make the cross-reference form inconsistent across the book.
findings.fix_instruction: Normalize every repeated-chapter pointer to the allowed form: e.g. "Ch. 2 §1.1" or "§2.1.1"; "Ch. 4 §8" or "§4.8"; "Ch. 7 §8" or "§7.8"; "Ch. 4 §3" or "§4.3"; "Ch. 8 §3.3.3" or "§8.3.3"; "Ch. 8 §7" or "§8.7". Sweep the whole manuscript for the same pattern.

findings.evidence: "A single token can be a whole word (handbook), a common subword (hand), a single character, a short punctuation+space pair, or in worst cases a single byte (a fragment of a character)." and §1.1.1: "the 'one token ≈ 4 characters' rule of thumb is for rough estimation of general-English prose, never a law" [2°][FACT].
findings.issue: The [2°][FACT] label on the '4 characters ≈ 1 token' rule of thumb (p.27) claims a reputable second-hand source states it as fact, but no source is named inline or in a footnote for this specific claim anywhere in Chapter 1 (the only [2°][FACT] nearby is about high-frequency English words rendering as single tokens, which is a different claim). A [2°][FACT] label without a traceable source is a provenance gap under the book's own rule that 'Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair' and that [2°] means 'reputable second-hand: textbook, survey, or independent benchmark' — the source must be identifiable.
findings.fix_instruction: Either cite the specific textbook/survey that states the ~4-chars-per-token heuristic (add an [S#] or footnote), or downgrade the label to [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] / [HYPOTHESIS] since the heuristic is a rough rule rather than a sourced fact.

findings.evidence: Page 28: "or, for non-autoregressive generation, in model evaluations (Ch. 2 §2.1.1; Ch. 3 §3.1.1 and Appendix A §9A)". Page 31: "for non-AR generation the same reasoning runs on model evaluations instead of output tokens, and Ch. 2 §2.1.1 (latent video) and Ch. 3 §3.1.1 (diffusion/LLaDA-style) carry the extension." Target check: page 38 headings "2.1.1. Table 2-1 — The resource model: seven resources..." vs page 40 heading "2.1.2. The work unit changes with the generator — Reader orientation (scope note). This subsection is a scoped aside on non-text generative workloads."
findings.issue: Both citations of "Ch. 2 §2.1.1" for the non-autoregressive/latent-video treatment resolve to the wrong subsection: §2.1.1 is the resource-model table (p. 18); the latent-video aside is §2.1.2 (p. 20). The pointers also use the form "Ch N §N.M", which the book's own convention (p. xv) forbids.
findings.fix_instruction: Change both occurrences to "Ch. 2 §2.1.2" (and, if the convention is enforced, to "Ch. 2 § 2" style or bare "§2.1.2").

findings.evidence: Page 34: "it is worked at Ch. 4 §4.8 and Ch. 7 §7.8." Page 49: "not the per-host aggregate rate of ~19,800 tok/s — see Ch 8 §8.3.4". Page 110: "(Ch 4 §4.8; Ch 17 Table 17-1)". findings.issue: Recurring malformed section references of the exact form the book's own reading conventions prohibit (chapter name followed by a chapter-numbered §N.M). At least five occurrences beyond the two counted in F02.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite as "Ch. 4 § 8" / "§4.8", "Ch. 8 § 3.4" / "§8.3.4", etc., per the p. xv convention; sweep the whole book for the "Ch N §N.M" pattern.

findings.evidence: (It is a computational/textual unit, not a unit of thought: two tokenizers can render the same semantic content in different token counts, and a reasoning model can spend very different compute per visible token.)
findings.issue: Terminology definition. The phrase 'unit of thought' is metaphorical and potentially misleading for a technical handbook. It is used to distinguish token count from reasoning depth (which is a valid distinction), but the phrasing is slightly 'fluffy' compared to the rest of the book.
findings.fix_instruction: Rephrase to: 'It is a computational input unit, not a semantic unit: two tokenizers...'

findings.evidence: (This is the engine-configured maximum, not a law of physics — some models use sliding-window or rolling attention that retains only a bounded recent context...)
findings.issue: Forward Reference. This chapter is Chapter 1. It references 'sliding-window' and 'rolling attention' as mechanisms. These are defined in Chapter 7. The sentence is a parenthetical aside, which is acceptable, but for a 'first token' chapter, it might be premature.
findings.fix_instruction: Add a cross-reference marker like '(Ch. 7)' to the parenthetical statement.
